problems.problem:
There are $n$ cards, where $n\ge50$ is an integer. Each card has one black side and one blue side. Initially the cards lie in a row on a table, all showing their blue sides. Alberto and Barbara, standing on the same side of the table, take turns choosing a block of $50$ consecutive cards whose leftmost card is blue, and turning over all the cards in that block. Alberto starts. The game ends when no legal move is possible; the player making the last legal move wins.

(a) Prove that the game terminates for every $n$.

(b) Determine, in terms of $n$, which player has a winning strategy.

A cyclic quadrilateral has the property that the midpoints of its sides also form a cyclic quadrilateral. Prove that the area of the disk bounded by the circumcircle of the smaller quadrilateral is at most half the area of the disk bounded by the circumcircle of the larger quadrilateral.
Let $a,b,c$ be positive real numbers such that $$\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c=a+b+c.$$ Prove that $$\frac1{(2a+b+c)^2}+\frac1{(2b+c+a)^2}+\frac1{(2c+a+b)^2}\le\frac3{16}.$$
Find all solutions $(p,n;x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_p)$ of $$\sum_{i=0}^{p}x_i^{p!}=p^n,$$ where $p$ is prime, $n$ is a nonnegative integer, and $x_0\le x_1\le\cdots\le x_p$ are nonnegative integers.

A football tournament has $n\ge3$ teams. Each team plays each other team exactly once. A win earns $3$ points, a loss $0$ points, and a draw $1$ point for each team. At the end, all teams have distinct point totals forming an arithmetic progression, and the last-place team has exactly one point. Determine all possible configurations: the value of $n$, the final standings, and the results of every match.

In triangle $ABC$, an excircle touches side $BC$ at $D$ and the extensions of $AB$ and $AC$ at $E$ and $F$, respectively. Let $P$ be the perpendicular projection of $D$ onto $EF$, let $M$ be the midpoint of $EF$, and let $\Gamma$ be the circumcircle of $ABC$. Prove that $P$ lies on $\Gamma$ if and only if $M$ lies on $\Gamma$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle. The line parallel to $BC$ and tangent to the incircle meets $AB$ at $A_1$ and $AC$ at $A_2$. Define $B_1,B_2,C_1,C_2$ analogously. Prove that $$AA_1\cdot AA_2+BB_1\cdot BB_2+CC_1\cdot CC_2\ge\frac19(AB^2+BC^2+CA^2),$$ and determine the equality cases.

At a concert, $k$ singers are to perform one after another. Each singer specifies a possibly empty set of other singers and asks to perform after every singer in that set. Determine whether there can be exactly $2010$ performance orders satisfying all the requests in each of the following cases: (a) $k=80$; (b) $k=70$; (c) $k=20$.
Find the smallest positive integer $n$ for which there exist polynomials $p_1(x),\ldots,p_n(x)$ with rational coefficients such that $$x^2+7=[p_1(x)]^2+\cdots+[p_n(x)]^2.$$

Let $n>1$ be odd. Let $S$ be the set of integers $k$ with $1\le k\le n$ that are relatively prime to $n$, and let $T$ be the set of $k\in S$ for which $k+1$ is relatively prime to $n$. For each $k\in S$, let $r_k$ be the remainder on division by $n$ of $$\frac{k^{|S|}-1}{n}.$$ Prove that $$\prod_{k\in T}(r_k-r_{n-k})\equiv |S|^{|T|}\pmod n.$$

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral such that the lines $BC$ and $AD$ meet at $P$. Let $Q\ne B$ lie on line $BP$ and satisfy $PQ=BP$. Construct parallelograms $CAQR$ and $DBCS$. Prove that $C,Q,R,S$ lie on a circle.

Let $x_1,\ldots,x_{100}$ be nonnegative real numbers satisfying $x_i+x_{i+1}+x_{i+2}\le1$ for every $i=1,\ldots,100$, with indices taken modulo $100$ so that $x_{101}=x_1$ and $x_{102}=x_2$. Find the maximum possible value of $$S=\sum_{i=1}^{100}x_ix_{i+2}.$$

Determine whether there exists a sequence $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ of positive integers satisfying both of the following conditions: $$a_{n+1}=a_n+\tau(n)\quad\text{for every }n\ge1,$$ where $\tau(n)$ is the number of positive divisors of $n$; and at least two consecutive terms of the sequence are perfect squares.

A convex $n$-gon is triangulated by diagonals that do not intersect inside the polygon. Each triangle is coloured white or black, with triangles sharing a side always having different colours. Determine, in terms of $n$, the greatest possible difference between the number of white triangles and the number of black triangles.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with circumcentre $O$ and circumcircle $\Gamma$. Let $D$ lie on segment $BC$, distinct from its endpoints and midpoint. The circumcircle of $BOD$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $K$ and line $AB$ again at $E$. The circumcircle of $COD$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $L$ and line $AC$ again at $F$. The circumcircle of $AEF$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $M$. Suppose that $E$ lies inside segment $AB$ and $F$ inside segment $AC$. Prove that triangles $ABC$ and $MKL$ are congruent.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let $\ell$ pass through its circumcentre parallel to the bisector of angle $A$. Prove that $\ell$ passes through the orthocentre of $ABC$ if and only if $AB=AC$ or $\angle BAC=120^\circ$.

Consider $$P(x)=(x+d_1)(x+d_2)\cdots(x+d_9),$$ where $d_1,\ldots,d_9$ are nine distinct integers. Prove that there is an integer $N$ such that for every integer $x\ge N$, $P(x)$ is divisible by a prime greater than $20$.

For a function $f$ from a set to itself and a positive integer $k$, write $f^{(k)}$ for its $k$th iterate, defined by $f^{(1)}(x)=f(x)$ and $f^{(k+1)}(x)=f(f^{(k)}(x))$.

(a) Find all functions $f$ from the positive integers to the positive integers such that $$f^{(n+1)}(n)<f(n+1)$$ for every positive integer $n$.

(b) Find all pairs $(f,g)$ of functions from the positive integers to the positive integers such that $$f^{(g(n)+1)}(n)+g^{(f(n))}(n)=f(n+1)-g(n+1)+1$$ for every positive integer $n$.

Let $n>m>0$ be integers. Determine, in terms of $n$ and $m$, the greatest possible value of $x_1^2+\cdots+x_m^2$ among all $n$-tuples of real numbers $0\le x_1\le\cdots\le x_n$ satisfying $x_1+\cdots+x_n=1$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB\ne AC$ and circumcentre $O$. Let the angle bisector from $A$ meet $BC$ at $D$, and let $E$ be the reflection of $D$ in the midpoint of $BC$. The perpendicular to $BC$ through $D$ meets line $AO$ at $X$, and the perpendicular to $BC$ through $E$ meets line $AD$ at $Y$. Prove that $BXCY$ is cyclic.

Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be nonzero polynomials with integer coefficients and $\deg f>\deg g$.

(a) Suppose that $pf(x)+g(x)$ has an integer root for infinitely many primes $p$. Prove that $f(x)$ has an integer root.

(b) Suppose that $pf(x)+g(x)$ has a rational root for infinitely many primes $p$. Prove that $f(x)$ has a rational root.

Call a set $A$ of integers plump if, for every $x,y\in A$, possibly equal, and every integer $k$, we have $x^2+kxy+y^2\in A$. Find all pairs of integers $(m,n)$ for which the only plump set containing both $m$ and $n$ is $\mathbb Z$.

For every positive integer $n$, let $C(n)$ be the largest integer $k$ for which there are $k$ disjoint pairs of elements of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ whose pair sums are $k$ distinct integers at most $n$. Each pair contains two distinct elements, and no element belongs to more than one pair.

(a) Determine $C(12)$ and $C(13)$.

(b) Determine $C(n)$ for every positive integer $n$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral. Circle $\Gamma_1$ passes through $A,B$ and is tangent to side $CD$ at $E$. Circle $\Gamma_2$ passes through $B,C$ and is tangent to side $DA$ at $F$. Circle $\Gamma_3$ passes through $C,D$ and is tangent to side $AB$ at $G$. Circle $\Gamma_4$ passes through $D,A$ and is tangent to side $BC$ at $H$. Prove that $EG$ and $FH$ are perpendicular.

Define a sequence $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ by $a_1=a_2=1$ and, for every $n\ge1$, $$a_{2n+1}=2a_{2n}-a_n,\qquad a_{2n+2}=2a_{2n+1}.$$ Prove that $a_n$ is divisible by $5$ whenever $n>3$ and $n-3$ is divisible by $8$.
Let $p$ be prime, and let $(x_1,\ldots,x_p)$ be a $p$-tuple of integers such that $$x_1^n+\cdots+x_p^n\equiv0\pmod p$$ for every positive integer $n$. Prove that $x_1\equiv\cdots\equiv x_p\pmod p$.

Let $\omega_1$ be a circle with centre $O$, let $AB$ be a diameter, and let $C\in\omega_1$ satisfy $90^\circ<\angle AOC<180^\circ$. Let $K$ lie on line $OC$ with $C$ between $K$ and $O$, and let $\omega_2$ have centre $K$ and pass through $C$. Let $E$ be the other intersection of line $KB$ with $\omega_1$, and let $S,T\in\omega_2$ be the points for which $ES$ and $ET$ are tangent to $\omega_2$. Prove that lines $AC,EK,ST$ are concurrent.

Let $A_0B_0C_0$ be a triangle of area $\sqrt2$ in the Cartesian plane. Let the vertices of $A_1B_1C_1$ be the excentres of $A_0B_0C_0$, let the vertices of $A_2B_2C_2$ be the excentres of $A_1B_1C_1$, and continue in this way. Determine whether this procedure can eventually produce a triangle whose vertices all have both coordinates rational.

A mathematics competition has $30$ contestants and $8$ problems. Each problem is either solved or not solved. After the competition, the value of each problem is set equal to the number of contestants who did not solve it: for example, a problem solved by everyone is worth $0$ points, and one solved by $8$ contestants is worth $22$ points. Each contestant receives the sum of the values of the problems they solved. There is a unique last-place contestant, whose score is strictly below everyone else's. Find the largest possible score of this contestant.
Let $a,b,c,p,q,r$ be positive integers satisfying $$a^p+b^q+c^r=a^q+b^r+c^p=a^r+b^p+c^q.$$ Prove that $a=b=c$ or $p=q=r$.
Determine whether there exists a function $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ such that $$(x^2+y)f(yf(x)+f(y^2))=x^3f(y^2f(x))$$ for all positive real numbers $x,y$.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral. Lines $AD$ and $BC$ meet at $E$, and diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ meet at $P$. The circumcircles of $APD$ and $BPC$ meet again at $Q$. Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of $AD,BC$, respectively, and let $K=AC\cap MN$ and $L=BD\cap MN$.

(a) Prove that $EMQN$ is cyclic.

(b) Prove that the circumcircles of $AMK$ and $BNL$ pass through $Q$.

(c) Prove that these two circles pass through a common point on line $AB$.

Let $n\ge2$ be an integer, and let $$A_n=\{2^n-2^k:k\in\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}\}.$$ Determine, in terms of $n$, the largest positive integer that cannot be written as a sum of one or more, not necessarily distinct, elements of $A_n$.

A country has $20$ cities and $18$ aeroplanes. Each aeroplane regularly follows a directed circular route of five legs visiting five distinct cities. Each city is visited by the routes of at least three aeroplanes. For each pair of cities, at most one aeroplane connects them directly, in either direction, without an intermediate stop. Prove that every city can be reached from every other city by using these flights appropriately.
Find all pairs of positive integers $(x,y)$ with the following property: whenever $a,b$ are relatively prime positive divisors of $x^3+y^3$, the number $a+b-1$ is also a divisor of $x^3+y^3$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB>BC$, circumcentre $O$, and circumcircle $\Omega$. Let $M$ be the second intersection of the angle bisector from $B$ with $\Omega$, let $K$ be the midpoint of $BM$, and let $\Gamma$ be the circle with diameter $BM$. The bisector rays of $\angle AOB$ and $\angle BOC$ meet $\Gamma$ at $P$ and $Q$, respectively.

(a) Prove that $PQKO$ is cyclic.

(b) Let $R$ be the point on line $PQ$ satisfying $RB=RM$. Prove that $BR$ and $AC$ are parallel.

Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with an interior point $P$ such that $\angle APD=\angle BPC=90^\circ$ and $PA\cdot PD=PB\cdot PC$. Let $O$ be the circumcentre of $CPD$. Prove that line $OP$ passes through the midpoint of $AB$.

On a certain day, $2016$ customers visited a shopping centre. Each entered once, stayed for some time, and then left without returning. A group is called simultaneous if all its members were inside the shopping centre together at some instant. A group is called sequential if no two of its members were inside together, even for an instant. Find the largest integer $k$ such that, regardless of the arrival and departure times, there must be a simultaneous group of at least $k$ customers or a sequential group of at least $k$ customers.
Prove that there is no function $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ such that $$f(f(x)+y)=f(x)+3x+yf(y)$$ for all positive real numbers $x,y$.
Let $a,b$ be positive integers such that $a!+b!$ divides $a!\cdot b!$. Prove that $3a\ge2b+2$.
Let $(a_n)$ be a sequence of positive real numbers such that $$a_{n+1}\ge\frac{na_n}{a_n^2+(n-1)}$$ for every positive integer $n$. Prove that $a_1+\cdots+a_n\ge n$ for every $n\ge2$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB\ne AC$, and let $D,E,F$ be the midpoints of $BC,CA,AB$, respectively. Let $\omega$ pass through $A$ and be tangent to line $BC$ at $D$. Circle $\omega$ meets line $AB$ again at $X$, line $AC$ again at $Y$, line $DE$ again at $R$, and line $DF$ again at $S$. Let $X\prime$ be the reflection of $X$ in $F$, and $Y\prime$ the reflection of $Y$ in $E$. Line $X\prime Y\prime$ meets line $AD$ at $Q$ and line $EF$ at $M$. Finally, let $P$ be the other intersection of $\omega$ with line $AM$.

(a) Prove that $R,S$ lie on line $X\prime Y\prime$.

(b) Prove that $Q$ lies on the radical axis of the circumcircles of $DCR$ and $DBS$.

(c) Prove that $AQ=QP$.
Find all functions $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that $$f(a^2)-f(b^2)\le(f(a)+b)(a-f(b))$$ for all real numbers $a,b$.

(a) Find all triples $(a,b,n)$ of positive integers with $n\ge2$ such that $n^{a+b}-1$ is a multiple of $n^a+n^b+1$.

(b) Find all triples $(a,b,n)$ of positive integers with $n\ge2$ such that $n^{a+b}-1$ is a multiple of $n^a+5n^b+1$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB=AC\ne BC$ and incentre $I$. Line $BI$ meets $AC$ at $D$. The line through $D$ perpendicular to $AC$ meets $AI$ at $E$. Let $J$ be the reflection of $I$ across line $AC$. Prove that the circumcircle of $BED$ passes through $J$.
Find all functions $f:\mathbb Z_{>0}\to\mathbb Z_{>0}$ such that $$xf(x)+[f(y)]^2+2xf(y)$$ is a perfect square for all positive integers $x,y$.

Let $n\ge5$ be an integer relatively prime to $6$. The vertices of a regular $n$-gon are coloured with three colours, with an odd number of vertices of each colour. Prove that there is an isosceles triangle whose vertices have three different colours.
Find all positive real numbers $\alpha$ for which there exists a strictly increasing sequence $(x_n)$ of positive integers such that $$x_{2n}+x_{2n-1}=\alpha x_n$$ for every positive integer $n$.

A rectangle $R$ has side lengths that are odd positive integers. It is partitioned into smaller rectangles, all with integer side lengths. Prove that at least one smaller rectangle has the property that the distances of its sides from the corresponding sides of $R$ are either all even or all odd.

A sequence $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ of real numbers satisfies $$a_n=-\max\{a_i+a_j:i+j=n\}$$ for every $n\ge2018$, where $i,j$ are positive integers. Prove that the sequence is bounded: there is a real number $M$ such that $|a_n|\le M$ for every positive integer $n$.

Call a rational number terminating if its decimal expansion has only finitely many nonzero digits. For every positive integer $m$, let $S(m)$ be the set of positive integers $k$ for which there exists $c\in\{1,2,\ldots,2018\}$ such that $$k=\min\left\{i\ge1:\frac{10^i-1}{cm}\text{ is a terminating rational number}\right\}.$$ Find the largest possible number of elements of $S(m)$ as $m$ ranges over the positive integers.

Let $p$ be prime. Alberto and Barbara take turns forming a decimal number with $p$ digit positions, allowing leading zeroes. On each turn, the player chooses a position not previously chosen by either player and places a digit from $0$ to $9$ in it. Alberto moves first. Alberto wins if the final number is divisible by $p$; otherwise Barbara wins. Prove that Alberto has a winning strategy.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle. The $A$-excircle $\omega$ touches side $BC$ at $D$, line $AC$ at $E$, and line $AB$ at $F$. The circumcircle of $AEF$ meets line $BC$ at $P,Q$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AD$. Prove that the circumcircle of $MPQ$ is tangent to $\omega$.

Let $S$ be a finite set, let $F$ be the set of all functions from $S$ to $S$, and let $f\in F$. Write $T=f(S)=\{f(x):x\in S\}$. Suppose that for every $g\in F$ with $g\ne f$, there exists $s\in S$ such that $$f(g(f(s)))\ne g(f(g(s))).$$ Prove that for every $t\in T$ there exists $x\in T$ such that $f(x)=t$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle, and let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $A$. The circle with centre $A$ passing through $D$ meets the circumcircle of $ABC$ at $X,Y$, where $X$ lies on the same side of line $AD$ as $B$. Prove that $\angle BXD=\angle CYD$.

Let $a_0,a_1,\ldots$ be a sequence of positive integers such that, for every $n\ge1$, $a_n$ is the smallest positive integer for which $a_0+a_1+\cdots+a_n$ is divisible by $n$. Prove that there exists a positive integer $m$ such that $a_n=a_m$ for every $n\ge m$.

Define $(a_n)_{n\ge0}$ by $$a_n=2^n+2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.$$ (a) Prove that infinitely many terms of this sequence can be written as a sum of two or more distinct terms of the same sequence.

(b) Prove that infinitely many terms of the sequence cannot be written as a sum of two or more distinct terms of the same sequence.
Find all pairs of positive integers $(a,b)$ for which there exists a positive integer $n$ such that $na$ and $nb$ have the same number of positive divisors.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB=AC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Let $P$ be a point such that line $PA$ is parallel to line $BC$ and $PB<PC$. Let $X$ lie on line $PB$ and $Y$ on line $PC$ such that $B$ lies on segment $PX$, $C$ lies on segment $PY$, and $\angle PXM=\angle PYM$. Prove that $APXY$ is cyclic.

Find the largest integer $k$ with the following property: whenever a $5\times5$ array is filled with the integers $1,2,\ldots,25$, each used exactly once, there is a $2\times2$ square of adjacent cells whose entries have sum at least $k$.
